Seated or standing he is the same man at the same size, his head as large when he sits as when he stands, and his face the same man's face, as long and as square-jawed, never rounder or younger when he sits or chews. His round hands are the same size in every view, in profile too. His skin warm peach (#f2b27c, its shade turned toward a rosy violet #c9877e), his small round ears showing at the sides of his head. Short curly brown hair (#6c432b, its shade a deeper violet-brown #57384a) kept close to his head, a soft rounded cap of small curls that adds little height above his brow and stands out no further than his ears, which show below it, covering the top of his head and its sides down to his ears, never long and never to his shoulders, never a big round puff; the curls sit at the same height above his brow and end at the same place beside his ears in every view; in profile the hair ends above and behind his ear, and below it his cheek and jaw are bare skin; no grey anywhere in his hair. No beard, no moustache and no stubble: his cheeks, jaw and chin are bare skin. His face is three marks: two short, thin, gently arched brows close over the eyes, never long, heavy or flat bars, a man's face as much as a boy's, two small dark oval eyes, each about an eighth of his face's height, and a one-line mouth in a small warm smile, upturned even at rest, no nose drawn and no crease lines beside the eyes. He is dressed in the Bible's own time, as every figure of this film is: a long cream tunic (#f2d8b7, its shade turned toward lavender #cbbfd2) to the ankles with long sleeves to the wrist, and over it one muted teal mantle (#58767a, its far side turned toward a deeper blue-violet #4f5f78, as coloured as the teal) worn over his left shoulder: it covers his left arm in a teal sleeve to the wrist, crosses his chest on a slant from his left shoulder down to his right hip, and hangs to his knees, so the cream tunic shows at his right shoulder and right sleeve, on his right side and below the mantle to his ankles; a cream cloth sash (#eadcc2, its shade turned toward lavender #c8bdd6) round his waist over the mantle, tied in a small knot at the front, its two ends hanging to his knees. Seen from his left side (a profile facing the viewer's left) the teal shows: his left sleeve is teal and the mantle hangs to his knees over the cream tunic; seen from his right side (a profile facing the viewer's right) the cream shows: his right sleeve is cream and the teal mantle is only a strip behind his shoulder; from behind, the mantle crosses his back from his left shoulder, on the viewer's left, down to his right hip. Brown sandals (#7a5236). A round warm-peach hand at the end of each sleeve, no thumbs, no fingers. No pattern, trim, embroidery, pockets or seams; no trousers and no shoes. He is not Christ: his hair short, no beard, his mantle teal, no white robe, no gold sash. What he carries, and only where a pose names it: a small plain baby's bottle with a pale teat and no markings; a plain wooden plate.

Draw only his head and the top of his shoulders, six times in a row, evenly spaced, all the same size. One to three are turned three-quarters toward the viewer's left: one, level, hopeful, the brows raised; two, level, wincing, the eyes squeezed and the mouth a tight wavy line; three, tilted a little, thinking. Four to six face the viewer straight on: four, level, at rest; five, level, wincing; six, lifted a little, tasting, the eyes closed in delight, a wide soft smile.

This is a model sheet for the animators, not a scene: a plain warm cream paper ground with a soft paper grain and no place behind, and nothing under the heads. Every head on the sheet is the same person at the same size: the same head size and the same hair, each head with the top of its shoulders only. No hands, no arms and no skin show below the neck. One thick warm dark-brown outline runs round the whole silhouette of each figure, and the head's outline is the one line inside it: none on the nose, the ear or the hairline, and the hair, the ear and the garments meet as flat colour, never as their own outlined pieces. The key light comes from the upper left on every figure, whichever way it faces, so its lit side is always on the left and its far side turns a deeper hue of its own colour toward violet, never grey and never black. Each turn is its own drawing, never a mirror of another. No lettering anywhere: no labels, no names, no numbers, no arrows, no text, no grid, no boxes or frames round the figures.
